To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“SMEs are able to assess the risks and benefits in open innovation projects by using a decision process framework and a software tool, which are developed and provided within the research project Open Darkness”.
SMEs are able to weigh the risks of engaging in open innovation projects by using the developed decision support framework and tool.

i) the weighing and decision process is structured by means of a process model and a software tool; ii) the software tool supports SMEs in the decision-making process; iii) the process model and the software tool enable SMEs to assess the risks and benefits associated with open innovation projects and to make a well-informed decision.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: i) How can a framework for weighing the pros and cons of open innovation participation be developed? ii) How can the framework be implemented as an automated tool? iii) How can the tool be applied to support SMEs to make informed decisions regarding open innovation project participation?

the development and application of a weighing and decision support process framework and tool for SMEs, in order to enable them to weigh the risks of open innovation project engagement and to make a well-informed decision.
the development of a weighing and decision framework and an associated software tool for SMEs to assess their ability to deal with the “dark sides of open innovation”.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
open innovation is not a panacea.

the research project “Open-Darkness” will enable SMEs to make informed decisions on whether or not they should participate in open innovation projects by developing a weighing and decision making process and a software tool that supports this process.

open innovation project participation can be a promising way for SMEs to improve their innovation performance, if they are able to deal with the challenges and risks of open innovation practice and to find an optimal balance of the pros and cons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an approach to help small and medium enterprises to make the right decisions in the context of open innovation.
we developed a software tool that allows SMEs to weigh risks and benefits of engaging in open innovation projects by using a decision process framework that was developed in the project.
we have developed a framework for decision making regarding participation in open innovation projects for SMEs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the decision dilemma of open innovation engagement can be tackled in a systematic manner by applying a weighing and decision framework and a corresponding software tool.
a systematic and holistic decision process for SMEs regarding open innovation participation is needed.
the decision to participate in an open innovation project is not only based on the expected benefits of the innovation project but also on the ability to cope with potential risks.
